story.name: ジャスミンの きっさてん
story.title: The Empty Shop by the Pier
story.line: ジャスミンが きっさてんを ひらこうと きめます
story.ja: ジャスミンは、桟橋のそばの空き家（昔のつりえさ屋）でカフェを開こうと決める。たぬきちに借りる話をして、ちゃちゃまるが掃除を手伝う。マスターに相談すると、ことばは少し。「小さく始めること。常連の名前をおぼえること。あせらないこと」。でも、いちばん大事なエスプレッソマシンを買うお金が足りない。

segments.en: At the end of the pier, past the place where the fishermen liked to sit, there was a little wooden building that nobody had used in years.
It used to be a bait shop. The paint was peeling, one window was cracked, and if you stood close enough, it still smelled faintly of fish.
Pekoe walked past it every morning on her way to the beach. And every morning, she slowed down a little more.
She had been making coffee and tea for her friends for years.
In her kitchen, on her porch, in a thermos on picnics. Everybody said she should open a café.
And every time, she laughed and said, oh, someday. But one morning in October, she stopped in front of the old bait shop and didn't keep walking.
Okay. Okay, Pekoe. It's now or never. You're going to go talk to Tom Nook. Today.
Tom Nook was behind his desk, as always, surrounded by papers and little stacks of leaf-shaped notes. He listened to her whole idea without saying a word.
A café by the pier? Yes, yes! I think that's a wonderful idea. The building does need a little work, though. Quite a bit of work, actually.
I know. I don't mind. I'll fix it up myself, little by little. Could I rent it month to month, just to start?
Of course. And the first month is on me. Think of it as a welcome gift. Every new business deserves a good start.
Pekoe walked out holding a big, old-fashioned key, and she held it so tight that it left a little mark on her paw.
The next morning, Dom showed up at the shop before she did. He had a mop, two buckets, and far too much energy for seven a.m.
Heard you're opening a café! I'm here to help. Cleaning counts as a workout, right? Let's do this!
They worked all day. They scrubbed the floor, took down the old fishing nets, and opened every window to let the sea air blow the smell away.
Under the nets, they found a long wooden counter, old and solid and beautiful.
Pekoe ran her hand along it and knew right away where the coffee would go.
That evening, tired and happy, she walked up to the museum to visit The Roost, the island's only café. Brewster was behind the counter, drying a cup.
Mr. Brewster, I'm opening a little café by the pier. I hope that's okay. I was wondering if you had any advice for me?
Brewster didn't answer right away. He finished drying the cup. He put it on the shelf. Then he dried another one.
Start small. Learn your regulars' names. And be patient. Coffee doesn't like to be rushed. Neither do people.
That was all he said. But Pekoe wrote it on a napkin, and later, she taped it to the wall behind the counter.
There was just one problem, and it was a big one. A café needs a coffee machine. A real one, with steam and pressure and shiny handles.
She looked through a catalog that night, curled up on her couch. Every machine she liked cost more than everything in her savings account.
Okay, so that one's way out of my price range. And that one. And, wow, that one costs more than the building.
She closed the catalog and looked out the window at the dark pier. The little shop was sitting there, clean and empty, waiting for her.
I'll figure something out. I always do. Just maybe not tonight.
And then she went to bed.
Down by the pier, the waves knocked softly against the posts, and the old shop, for the first time in years, did not smell like fish.

predict.ask: ジャスミンは どうやって マシンを 手に いれる？
choices: Brewster gives her his old machine from The Roost.
She saves up for a whole year before opening.
She buys a suspiciously cheap one from Redd.
predict.ja: つねきちから、あやしいほど安いマシンを買う。
